US companies are facing a massive debt maturity wall:

~$1.9 trillion in US speculative-grade corporate bonds and loans mature over the next 5 years, including $438 billion due by the end of 2028.

By comparison, in 2020, 2021, and 2022, this figure ranged from $1.4 trillion to $1.5 trillion.

The amount of junk-rated debt maturing within 2 years alone has surged +31% YoY.

At the same time, $1.6 trillion of investment-grade corporate debt is coming due by 2031.

Meanwhile, refinancing is becoming increasingly expensive, with the effective yield on publicly issued US junk debt rising +150 basis points over the last 12 months, to 8.0%.

The corporate refinancing burden is becoming a major issue.

BREAKING: The US personal savings rate fell -0.2 percentage points in September, to 4.2%, its lowest level since October 2022.

Since January 2024, this metric has declined -3.4 percentage points.

The personal savings rate is now well below the 5-year pre-pandemic average of 6.2%.

This comes as personal income grew +4.1% YoY in September, its 2nd-lowest growth rate since April 2022.

At the same time, personal consumption expenditures rose +6.3% YoY, the 2nd-highest YoY growth since December 2024.

In other words, consumer spending continues to outpace income growth, putting further pressure on household savings and increasing household reliance on borrowing.

Elevated inflation and record prices are putting further pressure on consumer savings.

a16z's Moses Sternstein and Alex Danco on the "rack spread," the gap between rising GPU prices and falling token prices:

"The core observation in the rack spread is as follows: roughly since the summer, GPU pricing has gone up, token pricing has gone down. Why that is: a combination of open competition, the labs themselves cutting prices."

"We start with a bunch of GPUs and a bunch of electricity and a bunch of cooling, and on the other side out comes tokens, right? And the thing that achieves that is the model."

"In an oil refinery, you have a bunch of inputs... It goes into a refinery, which is like the model, and then out come refined products that you can actually use, like jet fuel or diesel or lubricant or any number of specialized things."

"There is this term called the crack spread... It's not a net margin that anybody is actually making... But it is useful because if you look at any given refinery, just like you might look at any given model, you want to ask this basic question which is, 'Is this making any money?'"

@MosesSternstein @alex_danco

US corporate debt issuance is skyrocketing:

US investment-grade corporate bond sales are expected to rise +$37 billion YoY in November, or +27%, to $175 billion, the highest for any November on record.

This would mark a +$76 billion, or +77%, increase from November 2024 level.

To put this into perspective, the 5-year average before 2025 was $104 billion.

By comparison, US investment-grade bond issuance stood at ~$100 billion in October.

As a result, US investment-grade bond sales have risen to a record $1.76 trillion YTD, already surpassing the full-year 2025 total of $1.75 trillion.

Meanwhile, over $300 billion in AI-related corporate bonds have been issued in global investment-grade markets so far in 2026, almost 3 times the total for all of 2025.

AI spending is fueling an unprecedented wave of corporate borrowing.

There is a fundamental difference between the 2011 peak in silver and what we are seeing today.

Back then, rising prices were accompanied by a massive increase in production.

Today, that supply response is completely missing.

Don’t confuse a violent correction with the end of a cycle.

https://t.co/VDC5mLf0ag

thread_tweets.quoted_tweet_text:
AI productivity gains are showing up, but only in ~15% of jobs.

The three heaviest AI adopters (information, professional services, finance) went from a 2.2% productivity trend to 5.0% since 2022.

The rest of the economy: 0.9% to 1.4%. https://t.co/ZsdJ6lkkbC
